claims.text: The low-field magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of nanoscale, as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys are primarily governed by interfacial strain and grain-boundary effects.
Interfacial strain and grain boundaries alter magnetic phase-transition kinetics.
Reduced dimensionality limits efficient heat transfer in these films or nanoribbons.
The nanoscale alloy generally has a reduced magnetocaloric effect relative to bulk forms.
The as-deposited films or nanoribbons have high interfacial strain.
The as-deposited films or nanoribbons contain a dense grain-boundary network.
Controlled thermal annealing can relieve interfacial strain.
Controlled thermal annealing can modify the grain-boundary configuration.
Interfacial strain and grain-boundary density couple to magnetic-domain behavior during phase transitions.
Annealing-induced strain relief alters the nucleation and growth kinetics of magnetic domains.
Annealing-induced grain-boundary reconfiguration alters the nucleation and growth kinetics of magnetic domains.
The annealing-induced kinetic changes reduce magnetization hysteresis.
Annealing shifts the magnetocaloric-effect magnitude toward bulk values or otherwise changes it systematically.
Constrained heat transfer further modulates the magnetic and magnetocaloric effects, especially at higher cycling rates.
Under identical low-field conditions, annealed samples will have narrower hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline.
Under identical low-field conditions, annealed samples will have an increased or more stable magnetocaloric peak relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The magnitude of the magnetic changes will correlate with the degree of annealing-induced strain relief.
High interfacial strain and dense grain boundaries contribute to exaggerated hysteresis in the as-deposited baseline.
High interfacial strain and dense grain boundaries contribute to an atypical magnetocaloric response relative to bulk forms.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to bulk samples or thicker films because their strain and heat-transfer behavior differ markedly.
